paper.title: Using protein-per-mRNA differences among human tissues in codon optimization

generators.name: CUSTOM tissue codon generator
generators.description: Use the authors' released CUSTOM package to sample synonymous eGFP coding sequences from lung-specific codon probabilities.

evidence.quote: Therefore, for each amino acid, a certain codon is selected with a probability proportional to the first. If the selected codon is enriched in the tissue, it is incorporated into the sequence.
We applied CUSTOM to the protein sequences of eGFP and mCherry (Uniprot ID: C5MKY7, X5DSL3).

constraints.name: CUSTOM body MFE
constraints.description: Minimize the released CUSTOM mean 40-nucleotide sliding-window minimum free energy for the coding-sequence body.

evidence.quote: Minimum Free Energy (MFE): a measure of mRNA stability from the ViennaRNA package

constraints.name: CUSTOM initial MFE
constraints.description: Maximize the released CUSTOM minimum free energy of the first 40 nucleotides.

evidence.quote: CUSTOM distinguishes between the first 40 nucleotides (whose weak secondary structure leads to increased translation initiation) and the rest of the sequence (whose strong secondary structure relates to longer mRNA half-lives)

constraints.name: CUSTOM CAI
constraints.description: Maximize the released CUSTOM human codon adaptation index.

evidence.quote: Codon Adaptation Index (CAI): a measure of similarity between the codon usage of the sequence and that of the human genome

constraints.name: CUSTOM CPB
constraints.description: Maximize the released CUSTOM human codon-pair bias score.

evidence.quote: Codon Pair Bias (CPB): a measure of similarity between the codon pair usage of the sequence and that of the human genome

constraints.name: CUSTOM ENC
constraints.description: Minimize the released CUSTOM effective number of codons.

evidence.quote: Effective Number of Codons (ENC): a measure of codon evenness. A value of 20 means that all 100% codons are biased towards the most common codon, while 61 corresponds to no bias at all

optimizers.description: Generate one 1,000-sequence pool, min-max normalize the five metrics over that complete pool, filter homopolymers, and retain the top ten.

evidence.quote: Sequences were optimized to either lung or kidney, generating a total of n_pool = 1000.

assumptions: This reproduces the released in-silico eGFP-to-lung optimization, not the downstream cloning or expression experiment.

The five min/max directions are transcribed from the paper's displayed select_best call and confirmed against CUSTOM 0.0.1; Paperclip converts that formula to presentation markup, so the per-metric evidence quotes use the surrounding verbatim prose.
Each raw metric is mapped affinely into Proto's [0,1] score interval; affine mapping leaves the paper's per-pool min-max ranking unchanged.
The [-200,0] kcal/mol safety interval contains feasible ViennaRNA MFE values for every 40-nucleotide window and fails closed if violated.

Although ENC is interpreted on an idealized 20-to-61 scale, CUSTOM's finite-sequence estimator can slightly exceed 61; the [0,100] Proto affine envelope is a non-clipping transport bound, while the raw value and exact per-pool ranking are retained.
unknowns: The paper and released experiment script do not report random seeds, so the exact historical 1,000 candidate sequences cannot be regenerated.
The paper does not pin its CUSTOM, NumPy, pandas, or ViennaRNA dependency versions; this reproduction pins CUSTOM 0.0.1 and ViennaRNA 2.7.2.
Wet-lab expression measurements and the authors' final manual choice of two candidates are outside this computational reproduction.
